objective: Sequential focused-task campaign to improve validated learning efficiency and higher-order quantitative-research capability.
process_conclusion: Choosing this task produced a bounded, decision-relevant audit result with zero code change and zero regression risk. It did not produce the comparison the task asks for: the controller-side ordinal selector that exists today is not the mechanism that produced the cited frontier closures, and no durable record supports a rate comparison against the opportunistic era. Two genuine process observations beyond the contract's question: this is the first activation in the series to test the selector itself rather than exercise it, and its deliverable is a narrowing of the prior RETAIN rather than another demonstration. An independent read-only falsification review of this audit found two of its own supporting clauses over-stated (no-information-gain-classification; no duplicate terminal rows) and both were corrected here rather than suppressed; the review also surfaced two previously unrecorded defects in state/LEARNING_STATE.md itself (:30-32 malformed momentum row; :50-:51 duplicated regime-adaptive MA terminal row).
unverified: COMMAND-LEVEL BLOCKER: the bash tool is denied at this layer for every invocation (project permission rule). No script was executed, so no recomputation, regression run, or controller dry-run was performed for this audit; every finding above rests on direct repository-native reads. This is an execution-environment signal, not a research finding.

NO BASELINE MEASUREMENT: no durable document records experiments-per-decision or duplicate-experiment counts for the pre-contract era, so no rate comparison between opportunistic and frontier-first choice is computable from durable state. CORRECTED BY INDEPENDENT REVIEW: the stronger clause 'no per-activation information-gain classification exists' was FALSE as written. The Information Gain column of the learning-history table (state/LEARNING_STATE.md:44, :46, :50, :52) DOES classify the opportunistic-era activations (e.g. :44 'Framework capability established'; :46 'Methodology gap closed'; :50 'One MA-crossover rescue hypothesis eliminated with two independent paths'). It is retrospective and authored alongside the contract (logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-05.md:293-308) and has no denominators, so it does not rescue a rate comparison, but it is real evidence that the earlier clause wrongly denied. Durable wasted-work records also exist and cut both ways: logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-02.md:233-240 and state/STATE.md:487-489 (non-reproducible prior figures, 9/45 tests failing), logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-04.md:705-707, :736-738, :762-799 (execution blocked; 8/10 tests failing on first run), versus frontier-era rework at logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-05.md:540-548 (three check defects + one verifier defect), :618 (one verifier defect) and state/STATE.md:633-658 (four CSRS defects). Because rework is recorded in BOTH eras, wasted work cannot be pointed in either direction, which reinforces rather than weakens the no-comparison conclusion.

OBSERVATION IS SELF-REPORT: task_selection_observation in agent records is authored by the agent, not derived from evidence (evaluate_research_process.py lines 47-55 read the field verbatim; synthesize_campaign.py line 181 copies it verbatim). It cannot serve as an independent efficiency measurement without a cross-check that does not exist in the controller.

SCOPE CONFOUND: the frontier-first era added the a-priori falsification prediction, the independent verifier gate, determinism assertion, and manifest/preflight/leakage gates per activation (e.g. logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-05.md lines 680-697; logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-06.md lines 11, 50). The 'no equivalent re-tests' observation cannot be attributed to selection policy alone because evidence standards changed at the same boundary.

SELECTION MECHANISM (NOT MEASURED): this campaign selects work by controller-side ordinal ranking inside campaign_controller.py, whereas every cited historical cell records selection by a worker judgement of the frontier table (logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-06.md line 9: 'Selection basis: frontier-first'). The selector actually evaluated here is therefore not the mechanism that produced the five cited closures. No durable evidence links the controller selector's decisions to learning efficiency.
